overview: Two nuclear processes that both release enormous energy — one by splitting heavy nuclei, the other by combining light ones.
genZNote: Fission breaks up. Fusion teams up. Both release absurd amounts of energy either way.

aspects.label: Process
aspects.valueA: A heavy nucleus splits into two lighter nuclei, usually after neutron bombardment.
aspects.valueB: Two light nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus.

aspects.label: Conditions Required
aspects.valueA: Can occur at relatively moderate conditions (e.g. in a nuclear reactor with neutron moderation).
aspects.valueB: Requires extremely high temperature and pressure (as in stars, including the Sun).

aspects.label: Current Practical Use
aspects.valueA: Used in current nuclear power plants and weapons.
aspects.valueB: Powers stars; controlled fusion for power generation remains under active research/development.

aspects.label: Radioactive Byproducts
aspects.valueB: Produces comparatively little long-lived radioactive waste.
